question.text: In the PPM of Damodar Structured Credit AIF (Category II), the section on liquidity for close-ended AIFs states:

answer.text: Investors can redeem their units at any time like an open-ended mutual fund
Redemption is available quarterly at NAV minus a 10% exit load

Category I and II AIFs are close-ended and illiquid; investors may not be able to exit until winding up and distributions are completed, with any earlier exit routed through fund-document transfer/withdrawal practices or secondary-market sale of units or partnership interests
SEBI mandates a mandatory redemption window every 6 months for all AIFs

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook describes Category I and II AIFs as close-ended and illiquid: investors may not be able to exit until winding up and distributions are completed. Any earlier exit is governed by the fund's documented transfer and withdrawal practices (reviewed in the PPM audit) and through the secondaries route, which involves a sale of unit capital or partnership interests. Unlike open-ended mutual funds, there are no periodic redemption windows, and SEBI does not mandate quarterly redemption. The Trap: The quarterly redemption option borrows mutual fund concepts (exit loads, quarterly redemption) that do not apply to close-ended AIFs, which operate on a fundamentally different liquidity model. Note: Kept the close-ended/illiquidity key and rewrote the transfer language around source-backed secondaries and fund-document transfer/withdrawal practices. Removed the unsupported manager/trustee-consent framing and the pro-tip claims about a 5-10 year suitability range and illiquidity being the 'number one' source of investor dissatisfaction.
